78.0.0.en: 1- Give ear, O my people, to my law: incline your ears to the words of my mouth.

78.0.1.en: 1- God addresses His people, the children of Israel, and asks them to give ear, that is, to listen attentively, and to incline their ears humbly to His words and His Law; for the words are the words of God which He gave to Moses and the prophets, and therefore they are the most important words and need to be heard with humility, so that we may receive and understand the word of God.

78.0.2.en: 2- This verse speaks by the spirit of prophecy about Christ, who calls His Apostles, His priests, His servants, and indeed all His people, to hear the words of the New Testament which complete what was said in the Old Testament, as He declared in the Sermon on the Mount (Mt 5-7).

78.1.0.en: 2- I will open my mouth in a parable: I will utter dark sayings of old:

78.1.1.en: 1- God informs His people through the psalmist, speaking by way of parables, because a parable makes the idea clear in a practical way, so that it is close to the heart, as Christ did in the New Testament; in addition to God's making His prophets a means of declaring and clarifying His word through what they do, that they may be an example before their people, as happened with Jeremiah, Ezekiel, Hosea... A parable is hard for a person to reject, whereas direct speech may be rejected, because it shows the faults of its hearers plainly.

78.1.2.en: 2- God also declares His word in dark sayings, meaning that in addition to the simple, understandable speech given by way of a parable, God will also give deep speech, hard to grasp in all that it contains, so that a person grasps some of the meanings of God's word; for he finds himself before dark sayings, and as he reads them he gradually discovers new meanings, and so he lives by them and is satisfied. The word "dark sayings" written here means, in the original Hebrew, the mysteries; that is, God's word is full of deep meanings like mysteries, which He reveals to a person gradually.

78.2.0.en: 3- Which we have heard and known, and our fathers have told us. 4- We will not hide them from their children, shewing to the generation to come the praises of the LORD, and his strength, and his wonderful works that he hath done. 5- For he established a testimony in Jacob, and appointed a law in Israel, which he commanded our fathers, that they should make them known to their children: 6- That the generation to come might know them, even the children which should be born; who should arise and declare them to their children:

78.2.1.en: 1- The reports that the psalmist wants to declare to us, he heard and knew from the first fathers of God's people, and the fathers told them to their children, and the children in turn taught them to their own children, until they reached the generation of the psalmist. And these reports contain the teaching of praising God and worshiping Him, and glorifying Him for His mighty works and His wonders with His people.

78.2.2.en: 2- God set up the Tabernacle of Testimony, that is, the Tabernacle of Meeting that contains the Ark of the Covenant of God, in the midst of His people, the descendants of Jacob, and He also gave them His Law that they might live by it. When he mentions "Jacob", he means the one who took hold of his brother's heel and held him, and it is a symbol of spiritual striving. And when he mentions "Israel", he means the one who saw God at Peniel (Gen 32:31). So he calls his people to hold fast to striving, and then they receive the grace of seeing God. For God loves His people and reveals Himself to them and dwells in their midst in the Tabernacle of Meeting, and wants to show them Himself if they strive spiritually and hold fast to His commandments and laws. All this was fulfilled in the New Testament when Christ became incarnate and was born in the midst of His people the Jews, and showed them Himself by great signs and teachings, that they might believe in Him and be saved.

78.2.3.en: 3- The psalmist makes clear that believers in God are responsible to tell their children, that is, the following generations, and to make known to them who God is, and His commandments and His laws, so that they too may tell their children and teach them these things, until the fullness of time comes and Christ becomes incarnate and accomplishes our salvation on the Cross, and the Apostles go out, and all their successors, the priests and servants, to preach to the world and to hand on the faith from generation to generation until today. This teaching and handing on is what we call Holy Tradition, that is, the oral teaching of the faith and how we live it, which we received from the Fathers and give to our children after us, and which St. Paul the Apostle calls the deposit (2 Tim 2:2.)

78.3.0.en: 7- That they might set their hope in God, and not forget the works of God, but keep his commandments: 8- And might not be as their fathers, a straying and rebellious generation; a generation that set not their heart aright, and whose spirit was not faithful to God.

78.3.1.en: 1- If the children receive the faith and sound teachings from the fathers, this draws them to rely on God and not on themselves, and they hold fast to God's commandments and live by them.

78.3.2.en: 2- The children guard themselves against the evil conduct that their fathers followed, as follows:

78.3.3.en: a- "A straying generation": that is, apostate from the faith, as the fathers did by their worship of the golden calf (Ex 32:4).

78.3.4.en: b- "And rebellious": that is, murmuring and rebelling against God, as the children of Israel murmured many times in Sinai.

78.3.5.en: c- A generation that set not their heart aright: that is, they betrayed God and tried to kill Moses and Aaron several times (Num 16:42) and tried to return to Egypt (Num 14:4).

78.3.6.en: d- "Whose spirit was not faithful to God": that is, their intention was not pure and their heart was not sincere, but they were hypocrites who pretended to follow God while their hearts were attached to the lusts of the world.

78.3.7.en: In sum, he means that the children should be obedient to God and submissive to His commandments, walking with Him with a pure heart and worshiping Him faithfully.

78.3.8.en: Remember God's past works with you, that your faith may be established and you may rely on Him, and the lusts of the world cannot entice you, and so you will be with Him with all your heart.

78.4.s.en: (2) The works of G in Egypt and Sinai

78.4.0.en: . 9- The children of Ephraim, being armed, and carrying bows, turned back in the day of battle. 10- They kept not the covenant of God, and refused to walk in his law;

78.4.1.en: Armed (literally "drawers of the bow"), carrying bows: those who pull the string of the bow in order to aim their arrows.

78.4.2.en: 1- He speaks of the sons of the tribe of Ephraim, famous for their large number and their strength in war, who relied on themselves and not on God. These turned back in the war and did not stand firm before the Assyrians, who took them captive as slaves. The captivity of the tribe of Ephraim took place before the other tribes. And what may be meant by Ephraim is the whole kingdom of Israel, since it was the largest in number, so it was a symbol of the whole northern kingdom of Israel, which worshiped idols and departed from the worship of God in His temple in Jerusalem.

78.4.3.en: 2- Ephraim did not keep God's covenant and Law, and did not obey His commands to drive out the Canaanites, the original inhabitants of the land, when they entered the land of Canaan and took possession of it in the days of Joshua (Josh 16:10).

78.5.0.en: 11- And forgat his works, and his wonders that he had shewed them. 12- Marvellous things did he in the sight of their fathers, in the land of Egypt, in the field of Zoan. 13- He divided the sea, and caused them to pass through; and he made the waters to stand as an heap.

78.5.1.en: Zoan: an ancient Egyptian city that was called Tanis, where Pharaoh used to reside; it is in the Sharqia governorate, that is, east of the Delta, and its place now is the village of "San el-Hagar".

78.5.2.en: Nad (heap): a like and a counterpart.

78.5.3.en: 1- What caused the breaking of Ephraim, or Israel, was their forgetting of God's deeds and His power with their fathers when they were in the land of Egypt, when Moses met Pharaoh in Zoan, and God brought the ten plagues upon Pharaoh. And when his heart was hardened and he went out after God's people and caught up with them at the Red Sea, Moses struck the sea and divided it, and the waters of the sea stood to the right and to the left like a wall, and the children of Israel crossed into the wilderness of Sinai; but Pharaoh and his army, when they followed God's people, were drowned in the Red Sea.

78.5.4.en: 2- The waters also stood like a heap in the River Jordan in the days of Joshua when the Ark of the Covenant of God entered the river, and the people crossed to the other bank, into the land of Canaan.

78.6.0.en: 14- In the daytime also he led them with a cloud, and all the night with a light of fire.

78.6.1.en: 1- After the ten plagues with which God struck the Egyptians, and they allowed the children of Israel to leave Egypt, God did many miracles with His people, the first of which is that He appeared to them by day in a pillar of cloud that shaded them, so that the sun did not burn them. At the same time the pillar of cloud moves in front of them, and they move with it and it leads them, and this is a symbol of God's work in protecting His children from the trials that the sun symbolizes, and His guiding them in the way of life by His Holy Spirit.

78.6.2.en: 2- And the rest of this wonder is that the pillar of cloud by day turns at night into a pillar of fire stretching from the earth to heaven, and goes before the people to light their way, to dispel the darkness of the night, and to guide them to the way that God wants for them. The pillar of fire is a symbol of the work of the Holy Spirit who enlightens and guides the children of God to the way of the Kingdom, dispels the darkness of sin, burns up all evil, and protects them, as He separated between them and the army of Pharaoh when they crossed the Red Sea.

78.7.0.en: 15- He clave the rocks in the wilderness, and gave them drink as out of the great depths. 16- He brought streams also out of the rock, and caused waters to run down like rivers.

78.7.2.en: 1- The second miraculous work that God did with His people is that He gave them water to drink in the dry wilderness, the wilderness of Sinai, by making water burst out from the rock, so that much water came out and gave drink to all the people.

78.7.3.en: 2- He mentions the coming out of water from the rock twice because God repeated the bringing out of water from the rock in the wilderness many times, whether the people thanked Him, or doubted Him, or murmured against Him. We notice that the two words for rock mentioned differ in their Hebrew origin, and the text of the word for rock mentioned in v. 16 is the same as that mentioned in (Num 20:1-11), when the people doubted God and murmured against Him, but by His love and care He gave them water in abundance.

78.7.4.en: 3- The rock is a symbol of Christ, as St. Paul the Apostle said (1 Cor 10:4), and the rod with which he struck it is a symbol of the Cross, and the coming out of much water is a symbol of the Holy Spirit who gives drink to believers; in addition, the striking of the rock is a symbol of the piercing of Christ while on the Cross and the coming out of blood and water from His side.

78.8.0.en: 17- And they sinned yet more against him by provoking the most High in the wilderness.

78.8.1.en: The rebellion of the children of Israel against God was repeated in the wilderness of Sinai in spite of His great care for them through great miraculous works, the first of which was the ten plagues, then the pillar of cloud and the pillar of fire, and after that the dividing of the Red Sea, in addition to feeding them with manna and giving them water to drink from the rock. All this happened in very hard circumstances, that is, in the dry land, which is the wilderness of Sinai.

78.9.0.en: 18- And they tempted God in their heart by asking meat for their lust. 19- Yea, they spake against God; they said, Can God furnish a table in the wilderness? 20- Behold, he smote the rock, that the waters gushed out, and the streams overflowed; can he give bread also? can he provide flesh for his people?

78.9.1.en: They spake against God (literally "fell upon God"): they doubted God and rebelled against Him

78.9.2.en: 1- The children of Israel fell into two sins in their dealing with God in the wilderness of Sinai, namely:

78.9.3.en: a- Disobeying God, that is, not obeying His commands in refusing to enter the land of Canaan, and then their daring to enter the land of Canaan against the command of God, who had forbidden them because of the weakness of their faith, so their enemies defeated them, as appears in (v. 17).

78.9.4.en: b- Their tempting God, as appears in (vv. 18-20), because they doubted His ability to feed them meat, although they had seen His miracles and His ability to give them water to drink and then to feed them with manna.

78.9.5.en: 2- The sin of doubting God and tempting Him began in the heart, and then appeared in their words and their insolence against God.

78.9.6.en: 3- It is the right of the children of Israel, as children of God who believe in Him, to ask Him for food or for any need of theirs, and He will of course give it to them, but the sin was in:

78.9.8.en: b- Their lust and attachment to the meat and the foods which they used to eat in Egypt (Num 11:4-6).

78.9.9.en: 4- The children of Israel doubted God and His power when they said that He gave us water from the rock, for this water comes from the underground water in the earth, but can God give us meat?! That is, of course He cannot.

78.10.0.en: 21- Therefore the LORD heard this, and was wroth: so a fire was kindled against Jacob, and anger also came up against Israel;

78.10.1.en: God was greatly angry with them as a result of their ingratitude, and fire was kindled at the edge of the camp because of their murmuring, but the compassionate God heard the prayers of Moses for them and put out the fire (Num 11:1-3). Then after that He fed them much meat when flocks of quails came upon them.

78.11.0.en: 23- And he commanded the clouds from above, and opened the doors of heaven, 24- And had rained down manna upon them to eat, and had given them of the corn of heaven. 25- Man did eat angels' food: he sent them meat to the full. Doors: plural of misra' (the leaf of a door). Corn: wheat. Meat (zad): food. In spite of the murmuring and doubting of the children of Israel toward God, He poured His grace upon them and gave them manna from heaven, which is the bread of heaven, and therefore it was called "the corn of heaven." And this food He also called angels' food, because it came down from heaven, and St. Paul the Apostle even said of it that it was spiritual food (1 Cor 10:3), because it carries a special blessing, so that it satisfied the children of Israel not only bodily, but gave them reassurance that God was with them, and they rejoiced that they were eating from the hand of God, and so were satisfied spiritually.

78.12.0.en: 26- He caused an east wind to blow in the heaven: and by his power he brought in the south wind. 27- He rained flesh also upon them as dust, and feathered fowls like as the sand of the sea: 28- And he let it fall in the midst of their camp, round about their habitations. God did a great miraculous work with His people in the wilderness of Sinai in order to feed them meat, although their number was great, for they were about two million souls, since there were 600 thousand men besides women and children (Ex 38:26), to answer their murmuring and doubts, in that there were flocks of the quail bird (like the small quail) migrating from Africa northward, heading to Egypt and Sinai, and God sent upon these flocks an east wind coming from the Arabian Gulf that held them back from completing their journey, and also sent a south wind which collided with these flocks and drove them toward the children of Israel walking toward the wilderness of Sinai, and weakened the movement of these flocks, which numbered in the millions, so they flew close to the ground, at a height of a meter (Num 11:31). So it became easy for the children of Israel to catch these birds, which fly slowly, being weak as a result of the wind's colliding with them. And the Holy Bible describes their huge number as being like dust and like sand, and they flew around the tents in which the people dwelt.

78.13.0.en: 29- So they did eat, and were well filled: for he gave them their own desire; 30- They were not estranged from their lust. But while their meat was yet in their mouths, 31- The wrath of God came upon them, and slew the fattest of them, and smote down the chosen men of Israel. God proved His power to His murmuring, doubting people when He gave them meat in abundance, as the flocks of quails fell around their tents and they caught them easily, but they were not ashamed and did not repent of their sins; rather they rushed with their lusts to eat much of the meat greedily for a month (Num 11:20-22). And while they were immersed in their lusts and refusing to repent of their sins, the poisonous serpents attacked them and killed many of them, especially the fattest of them, that is, those who went furthest in their lust, and likewise the chosen men of Israel, that is, the strongest and the proudest and most self-exalting, for they are not those chosen by God, but those chosen in the eyes of the people. So the divine punishment attacked the people while the food was still in their mouths (Num 11:33, 34). And perhaps some of them killed themselves by eating too much, that is, by gluttony, so that they suffered indigestion and died, because they seized the opportunity of there being much meat which they might be deprived of and not find afterward in the wilderness because of their unbelief, and these are the ones he describes as the fattest.

78.13.1.en: God is able to do all things, and can give you everything you wish for, but I wish you would be occupied with His spiritual gifts more than the material ones. Enjoy being with God, and trust that He will give you all your material needs.

78.14.s.en: (3) The betrayal of the people of G in the wilderness and their forgetting His works

78.14.0.en: 32- For all this they sinned still, and believed not for his wondrous works.

78.14.1.en: God gave His people many wonders as we mentioned: He brought water out of the rock, manna came down from heaven, and the quails covered the camp where they lived, and in spite of this they sinned against God by their murmuring, their doubting, and their many lusts.

78.15.0.en: 33- Therefore their days did he consume in vanity, and their years in terror.

78.15.1.en: 1- God punished His people by making them wander in the wilderness forty years, so He wasted their time, and all the people who murmured against God died, so their journeying was in vain because they rejected God and murmured against Him. It was also in vain because of their disobedience, and their not benefiting from God's work with them, and their immersion in their vain lusts and their unbelief in God.

78.15.2.en: 2- God also consumed His people with terror because of their unbelief in Him and their fear that they would not find food, so they ate the quails greedily, and then the poisonous serpents attacked them, and they were very afraid, and indeed many of them died, but whoever believed in God and looked at the bronze serpent was saved from death. Then He consumed their life with terror when they continued in their unbelief, and so perished in eternal torment.

78.16.0.en: 34- When he slew them, then they sought him: and they returned and enquired early after God. 35- And they remembered that God was their rock, and the high God their protector.

78.16.1.en: When God punished the children of Israel for their lust for meat and killed them with the poisonous serpents, they were very afraid of Him and returned to Him, and prayed, and asked to submit to Him, for they knew that He was their strength (their rock), their protection and their shepherd (their protector). They even hastened to Him in prayer early in order to appease Him, but not with all their hearts, as will appear in the following verses.

78.17.0.en: 36- Nevertheless they did flatter him with their mouth, and they lied unto him with their tongues. 37- For their heart was not stedfast with him, neither were they faithful in his covenant.

78.17.1.en: 1- The return of the children of Israel to the Lord was outward, that is, their prayers were words from their mouths and not from their hearts, because lust remained in control of them and the love of God was far from them, and they forgot that God is the searcher of hearts and reins, and no one can deceive Him.

78.17.2.en: 2- So also in every generation we find these deceivers, like the heretics and innovators, who to this day lead people astray with their honeyed words, while they do not love God and do not submit to His commandments, and they draw the simple into their evil way.

78.18.0.en: 38- But he, being full of compassion, forgave their iniquity, and destroyed them not: yea, many a time turned he his anger away, and did not stir up all his wrath.

78.18.1.en: 1- In the face of man's evil, his rebellion, his doubting, and even his deceiving of God, we find on the other hand that God is compassionate and has pity on man; He is a father who is tender toward His children, so He forgives them their sins and stops His anger, and does not punish man, and if He is angry He punishes partially so that they may repent; for if His anger were kindled He would destroy man. And He makes excuses for man, because man is weak and his life is short like the wind that goes and does not return, that is, fades away; therefore when man sins God is long-suffering, giving him an opportunity to return to God.

78.18.2.en: 2- The teachers of the Jews consider (v. 38) to be the pivot of the whole Book of Psalms. For it lies in its middle, and shows God's love for man and His care for him.

78.19.0.en: 40- How oft did they provoke him in the wilderness, and grieve him in the desert! 41- Yea, they turned back and tempted God, and vexed the Holy One of Israel.

78.19.1.en: Vexed: that is, wearied Him and made Him suffer and bear their insults.

78.19.2.en: 1- God's long-suffering appears in His bearing His people's rebellion against Him many times in the wilderness of Sinai, for they grieved His heart. And they tempted Him many times and wearied Him by their rebellion (Num 14:22, 23), instead of delighting in His fellowship, since they are the only people in the world on whom God bestowed the favor of dwelling in their midst and caring for them on every side.

78.19.3.en: 2- All these insults the children of Israel directed to the holy God, forgetting His holiness and treating Him like an evil man, and rebelling against Him, and in this, without knowing it, they showed His holiness, which bears with rebellious sinners.

78.20.0.en: 42- They remembered not his hand, nor the day when he delivered them from the enemy. 43- When he set his signs in Egypt, and his wonders in the field of Zoan.

78.20.1.en: 1- The children of Israel did not remember God's work with them when He rescued them from the bondage of Egypt with great power, when Moses met Pharaoh in the city of Zoan, which is Tanis, which is in the Sharqia governorate. And God struck Pharaoh with the ten plagues at the mouth of Moses. These are great works that the whole world heard of, so how could God's people forget them, and return and rebel against Him, especially since God warned His people lest they forget His works with them (Deut 4:9).

78.20.2.en: 2- The hand of God that freed His people from bondage is a symbol of the Incarnation of Christ, who freed His children by His Cross from the bondage of sin.

78.21.0.en: 44- He turned their bays into blood, and their streams, that they could not drink. 45- He sent gnats among them, which devoured them; and frogs, which destroyed them.

78.21.1.en: Their bays: bays, plural of bay, which is a waterway that opens onto the sea from one side, so it differs from a canal that is open from both sides. What is meant by bays here is the branches of the Nile and the canals branching from it. Here he mentions some of the plagues with which God struck Egypt in order that His people might leave it, and the first of these plagues is the turning of the Nile into blood (Ex 7:17). The second plague is the frogs (Ex 8:2), and the third plague is the gnats (Ex 8:17).

78.22.0.en: 46- He gave also their increase unto the caterpiller, and their labour unto the locust. 47- He destroyed their vines with hail, and their sycomore trees with frost. 48- He gave up their cattle also to the hail, and their flocks to hot thunderbolts.

78.22.1.en: Caterpillar (jardam): one of the stages of the locust, which is the one that has not grown wings sufficient for flying, and it is very voracious in eating, and therefore its harm is very great in eating crops.

78.22.2.en: Hail: slabs of ice that fall from heaven with force and wound and kill the people and beasts that they meet, because they fall abundantly.

78.22.3.en: He also mentions a violent plague with which God struck the Egyptians, namely the plague of locusts, the eighth plague (Ex 10:12), then the plague of hail which killed people, beasts, trees and plants, which is the seventh plague (Ex 9:18). These two plagues were crushing for Egypt, for the locusts ate everything green, and the hail destroyed the trees of the rich, which are the vines, and those of the poor, which are the sycamores, in addition to the fact that sycamore wood was used in making the coffins in which the bodies of the dead were placed, and the Egyptians were very concerned with embalming and burying the dead.

78.23.0.en: 49- He cast upon them the fierceness of his anger, wrath, and indignation, and trouble, by sending evil angels among them.

78.23.1.en: 50- He made a way to his anger; he spared not their soul from death, but gave their life over to the pestilence;

78.23.2.en: The psalm tells us about God's discipline of the Egyptians, for He showed them His severe anger in the ten plagues, which showed them the weakness of their gods, and God's anger against them because of their evils. And the ten plagues were carried to them by evil angels; they are not evil in themselves, but on the contrary pure, but they carry harsh plagues, which the Egyptians consider an evil that befell them. The first nine plagues were a preparation for the tenth, harsh plague in which their firstborn were struck, and many died in the nine plagues, whether by pestilence or by the other various plagues; and He gave the plagues gradually, increasing in their severity, so He made a way for His severe anger that would appear in the tenth plague; all this so that the Egyptians might repent and believe in God and reject their weak gods. And some of them were affected and accompanied the children of Israel, and the Holy Bible called them the mixed multitude (Num 11:4).

78.24.0.en: 51- And smote all the firstborn in Egypt; the chief of their strength in the tabernacles of Ham:

78.24.1.en: At the end of the plagues came the harsh plague, which was the plague of killing all the firstborn of Egypt, of people and beasts. The firstborn are the first born, when the health of the parents is strong and their capacity for begetting is high, in addition to the fact that the firstborn is a pride to his parents; so the angel killed the strongest and proudest in Egypt, who are the descendants of Ham the son of Noah, and father of Mizraim (Gen 10:6).

78.25.0.en: 52- But made his own people to go forth like sheep, and guided them in the wilderness like a flock. 53- And he led them on safely, so that they feared not: but the sea overwhelmed their enemies.

78.25.2.en: After the Egyptians were struck with the ten plagues they were very afraid, so they begged the children of Israel to go out from their midst, and God led His people out from among them, and brought them across the Red Sea, and led them, and sustained them in the wilderness of Sinai. And so the strong, who are the Egyptians, became fearful, while the weak, who are the children of Israel, became safe; because God's power is with them, protecting them and caring for them.

78.26.0.en: 54- And he brought them to the border of his sanctuary, even to this mountain, which his right hand had purchased. 55- He cast out the heathen also before them, and divided them an inheritance by line, and made the tribes of Israel to dwell in their tents.

78.26.2.en: 1- After God had sustained His people in the wilderness of Sinai, He brought them in to possess the land of Canaan, and drove out from before them seven peoples stronger than His people, and settled His people in the cities and tents of these pagans, and He also called the land of Canaan the mountain of His sanctuary, because it was sanctified by God's presence among His people in it, and He also called it the mountain which His right hand had purchased; because the land of Canaan is full of mountains (Josh 14:12), among them the five mountains on which the city of Jerusalem was built and in which His holy temple dwelt. And He divided the land of Canaan among the twelve tribes, and areas of land were anciently measured by the line; all this was by God's power with His weak people, and God expresses His power by His right hand.

78.26.3.en: 2- In the New Testament Christ settles those who believe in Him in the place of the demons who fell from heaven, and their places were emptied, so that after the striving of this life the believers reign with Christ forever in heaven.

78.26.4.en: When you see those who wrong you being strong, do not be troubled by your weakness; for God's power is glorified in weakness, but hold fast to your prayers, and trust that God will protect you, and will even give you peace and joy in the midst of afflictions.

78.27.s.en: (4) Turning away from G in the age of the Judges

78.27.0.en: 59- When God heard this, he was wroth, and greatly abhorred Israel: 60- So that he forsook the tabernacle of Shiloh, the tent which he placed among men; 61- And delivered his strength into captivity, and his glory into the enemy's hand.

78.27.1.en: Shiloh: a place called Shiloh where the Tabernacle of Meeting settled in the land of Canaan for about three hundred years, after it had moved from Gilgal, and after that it settled in Jerusalem.

78.27.2.en: In the face of the ingratitude of God's people and their provoking Him by the worship of idols, God abandoned them and rejected them for a time until they should repent, and even refused to be in their midst, so the Philistines took the Ark of the Covenant of God, which was in Shiloh (1 Sam 4:1-11). And so God delivered His strength, which is the Ark of the Covenant of God, to the Philistines, and departed from His people.

78.28.0.en: 62- He gave his people over also unto the sword; and was wroth with his inheritance. 63- The fire consumed their young men; and their maidens were not praised. 64- Their priests fell by the sword; and their widows made no lamentation.

78.28.1.en: God continued His discipline of His people who worshiped idols and fell into many lusts, and He disciplined them by stirring up against them the original inhabitants of the land, when the children of Israel were negligent in driving them out and did not obey the word of God by the mouth of Joshua the son of Nun. So these peoples arose and occupied and enslaved the children of Israel, and killed many of them by the sword (1 Sam 4:10). And so the fire of God's anger consumed His people, and many of the men died in the fire of wars, so the maidens did not find anyone to marry them, and were not praised as they had been accustomed anciently to praise the bride on her wedding day. The priests also, many of them died, such as the two sons of Eli the priest, Hophni and Phinehas (1 Sam 4:11), and the widows also saw the calamity of the people, and the shock and fear came upon them, and they could not weep for their husbands, since the calamity of the people was too great for them to bear, so there was no room for receiving consolation or lamenting their husbands. The Book of Judges, and likewise First Samuel, is full of the disasters that came upon God's people.

78.28.2.en: God is long-suffering and gives you an opportunity to repent, so hasten and make use of it lest He abandon you, and many afflictions come upon you that are hard to bear. He loves you, so do not waste the opportunity of repentance, that you may enjoy His care.

78.29.0.en: 65- Then the Lord awaked as one out of sleep, and like a mighty man that shouteth by reason of wine.

78.29.1.en: Shouteth: crying out and calling aloud.

78.29.2.en: The psalm likens God to a man asleep from drinking much wine, who then awakes like a mighty man who shouts in a loud voice at the enemies of his people. The sleeper does not feel the time and thinks it short; so also God abandoned His people for a little while in order to discipline them, and then arose to discipline their enemies. All this shows God's love and care for His children. For He desires their repentance, and then defends them and protects them.

78.30.0.en: 66- And he smote his enemies in the hinder parts: he put them to a perpetual reproach.

78.30.1.en: 1- After God declared His anger against the enemies who wronged His people, He struck them a severe blow, so that they became a disgrace and a reproach among the peoples. This is what happened with the Philistines who struck the children of Israel, and God allowed this to discipline His people, and they stole the Ark of the Covenant of God, so God struck them with hemorrhoids (1 Sam 5:6, 7).

78.30.2.en: 2- When Christ rose like a mighty man from the dead He declared that Satan is bound, and freed those who believe in Him, and opened to them the Paradise of Joy.

78.31.0.en: 67- Moreover he refused the tabernacle of Joseph, and chose not the tribe of Ephraim: 68- But chose the tribe of Judah, the mount Zion which he loved.

78.31.1.en: 1- God honored the tribe of Ephraim, for He made its number large, since Ephraim is the son of Joseph. And He honored it also in that spiritual leaders came out of it, among them Joshua the son of Nun, and Gideon. But they did not keep His commandments, and became proud and rebelled, so He was angry with them and refused to dwell in their midst. So the Philistines took the Ark of the Covenant of God which was in Shiloh, which is situated in the tribe of Ephraim, and then the Ark returned from the Philistines to the village of Kiriath-jearim which is in the tribe of Judah, and then David moved it to Jerusalem. So God chose the tribe of Judah, from which would come Christ the Savior, and in it was the temple, and the tribe of Judah was more steadfast in the worship of God than the rest of the tribes.

78.31.2.en: 2- The Ark of the Covenant of God dwelt in the land of Canaan first in the city of Gilgal for a short period, then was moved to Shiloh in the tribe of Ephraim, and after this it was moved to Jerusalem, where the temple was built and the Ark placed in it, but the temple was burned by Babylon at the captivity, and then was destroyed in AD 70 by the Romans. And perhaps the moving of the Ark from Ephraim to Judah is a prophecy of God's rejection of the worship of the kingdom of Israel, which would separate from the tribes of Judah and Benjamin, and His acceptance of the worship offered in His temple in the tribe of Judah.

78.32.0.en: 69- And he built his sanctuary like the heights, like the earth which he hath established for ever.

78.32.1.en: After God moved the holy Ark to Jerusalem by the hand of David, He built there by the hand of Solomon a temple for Himself, like the holy heights in heaven where the angels are around the divine throne. And the building of Solomon's temple was a symbol of the Church, which is the earth that God established forever; because those who believe in God will live forever, and God will glorify them with Him in heaven.

78.33.0.en: 70- He chose David also his servant, and took him from the sheepfolds: 71- From behind the nursing ones he brought him to feed Jacob his people, and Israel his inheritance. 72- So he fed them according to the integrity of his heart; and guided them by the skilfulness of his hands. God chose David from among the tribe of Judah for his spiritual readiness, and he lived with God in perfection, after being tried in shepherding sheep, for it mentions that God took him from behind the nursing ones, that is, the mothers who care for their young attentively among the ranks of the sheep. So David was therefore able to shepherd God's people. And he shepherded them with skill and fatherhood, and with a perfect heart like the heart of God. He shepherded God's people Jacob, who is Israel, and was a symbol of Christ the Good Shepherd, who lays down His life for the sheep, and redeems His people on the Cross, to acquire them for Himself as sons in the Kingdom.

78.33.1.en: Obey God's commandments so that He may choose you from among His sons and work through you, and so that you may care for all who are around you, to draw them to Him, and you will enjoy His fellowship and His work in you.

78.33.2.en: The supplication to God the Deliverer "O God, the heathen are come into thine inheritance) ".. v. 1) Introduction:

78.33.3.en: 1- Its writer: Asaph, the chief of the singers in the days of David, and it may be that David himself is the writer, and he gave it to Asaph to sing.

78.33.5.en: A prophecy of the destruction of Jerusalem and the Babylonian captivity, or the devastation of the temple by Antiochus the Great in the days of the Maccabees, or the devastation of the temple by the Romans in AD 70.

78.33.6.en: 3- This psalm is a cry to God to rescue His people and His temple that was destroyed, and it is suitable for the Church and every believer to say if they pass through affliction.

78.33.7.en: 4- This psalm resembles Psalm 74, which speaks about the same subject, and one may refer to its introduction.

78.33.8.en: 5- This psalm is not found in the prayer of the Agpeya.
